text: For loops repeat a block of code, walking through a sequence one item at a time.
Range creates a sequence of numbers on demand — range of five gives you zero through four.
Notice it stops before five, just like slicing — the end value is never included.
You can also loop straight over a list, [cough] pulling out each fruit in turn.
Give range two arguments and it starts and stops where you say — one to four builds a little count.
Need the position along with the value? Enumerate hands you both the index and the item together.
[sniff] Range takes a third argument too, a step — here we count up by twos.
And loops can nest inside each other — an inner loop runs completely for every single pass of the outer one.
[laugh] That nesting is exactly how you'd walk through a grid, row by row and column by column.
Next video: while loops. Comment PYTHON if you want the cheat sheet.
